Project

The Project report provides a detailed profitability analysis for a specific project by comparing all income earned against expenses incurred.

This report helps you understand whether a project is profitable by calculating the net profit, which is the difference between total income and total expenses.

Use this report to evaluate project performance, make informed decisions about resource allocation, and assess whether projects are meeting their financial objectives.

Report Structure

The report is organized into two main sections that summarize all financial activity for the project:

Income - Shows all revenue generated by the project, grouped by income account. This includes sales invoices, receipts, and any other income transactions linked to the project.

Expenses - Shows all costs directly attributed to the project, grouped by expense account. This includes purchase invoices, payments, and any other expense transactions linked to the project.

The final line displays the Profit (or loss), which is calculated as total income minus total expenses. A positive value indicates a profitable project, while a negative value indicates a loss.

Time Period and Data Selection

The report automatically determines the time period based on the earliest and latest transaction dates for the project. This ensures all project-related transactions are captured regardless of when they occurred.

Only transactions that have been explicitly linked to this project are included in the calculations. Transactions without a project assignment will not appear in this report.

The report uses base currency amounts for all calculations, ensuring accurate profit calculations even when dealing with foreign currency transactions.

To learn more about creating and managing projects, see: Project — Edit
